institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a water specialization with an engineering approach to have a good balance and combination with the scientific approach seen at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *

questions.answer: We had an online introductory week to get information on libery access, campus classrooms, and others. It was very useful. Later, the  international team at BOKU prepared a city tour for all internaitonal to assist.

questions.answer: Off campus

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I also talked a lot with Austrian students and signed up for the Buddy program. This is useful to get the insight of the process and things that need to be considered when selecting a course at BOKU

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you first need to do the in-person registration at the host University and get your ID card, if not you are not able to register online for any course. So consider this and arrive at least 2 weeks before the courses start. Some courses have high demand, so if you can even get your BOKU ID before, the chances of getting to the courses you want are higher. If suddenly you see that a course is full, contact the professor and let him/her know that you are interested and what it can be done to increase the possibility of you getting in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Buddy program and Austrian students, in general, are happy to help as the BOKU system of courses is different than in other universities. So ask around. Courses at BOKU tend to overlap and depending on the type of course (lecture, exercise or combines) the requirements of assistance are different. All this is well explained by the international team at BOKU, but also do not be afraid of asking other students for insights.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered to all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be organised. As courses overlap and they start and end at different times, you need to be structured and understand the demanding of each course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took all master's courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You have different types of courses at BOKU, and depending on that the style also differs. Also, depending on the ECTS, which tends to be low hence you have to do a high number of courses to get to the 30 ECTS, whether you go in-depth on the topics or is more an overview. You can see all this on the course description on the BOKU online platform once you get your credentials (process that needs to be done in person unfortunately, so be aware of arriving before the classes start!)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master's thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Case studies in sanitary engineering and On-Site solutions for Water Supply and Sanitation. On the latter, the professors had a lot of onfield experience so it was rewarding to learn from them. The Case Study one was very hands-on, I chose a topic and work with a supervisor on investigating and doing a report to present at the end of the semester, I even organised my time as I wanted since we just had a meeting at the beginning of the semester to divide topics, and then met at the end to present the report. So it was a great modality and I went in-depth on sanitation in emergency situations, which is a topic I like.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had an unexpected cost but it was personal, I needed to go to see my family for a health emergency my father had.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, everything was as I expected as the International team at BOKU also gave information on this. To consider: the transport expense is not exactly real, in the sense that I bought the annual pass (as the semester pass for public transport was only for students under the age of 26). So I bought the annual transport pass which costs around 320 euros, so on that item, I put an approximate of that amount divided on the course of 12 month.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The international team at BOKU organises picnic and other fund activities like salsa dancing. So, despite COVID, there were some months when we had a lot of options to meet other international students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Picnic, salsa dancing, night outing, WhatsApp group to organise among ourselves, a city tour of the historic part of Vienna.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The city tour was amazing!! You got the chance to know more about Austrian history.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
There are towns you can go to for a day or weekend, like Merk, Hallstatt, and Graz. 
You also don't have to miss the Danube National Park (only accessible by bike)
Also, always check the internet as the Vienna Municipality organises a lot of events throughout the year (even in 2022 when COVID was an issue). We had Christmas Markets and an ice ring in winter. In summer music and film festivals outside :) It was lovely!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The challenge in Austria is the language. Outside BOKU hardly anyone speaks (or wants to speak) English. So this can bring difficulties in paperwork and communication with the government.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Austrian are in general very open, so try to make groups for the courses with them so that you get the chance to know them more closely.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language, as said before. The challenge in Austria is the language. Outside BOKU hardly anyone speaks (or wants to speak) English. So this can bring difficulties in paperwork and communication with the government.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The number of traditions they have, which are beautiful, the architecture, the local food, the music, dance and opera, and the history!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- You can easily get overwhelmed with the courses as they are a lot and the overlaps make you feel anxious all the time. If you are in general a self-demanding person, it will be hard not to only focus on the study part of the exchange. But try to give you time to also get to know Vienna and the city. So schedule daily work in the afternoon when you finish the courses, or something else. But make sure you make time for the cultural exchange as well as the academic one.
- Go to all the Christmas markets, do a tour of all the options the city had, and do not miss the ice skating ring in January at the Rathaus.
- In summer. google/ask for the schedule of activities, there are tons of free activities outdoors to do and do not miss going to the Danube canal for a swim! The local Vienna beach style :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If needed the international team at BOKU has weekly online consultation hours that you can find on the BOKU Website. So you can enter and have a quick chat with them for and they answer all questions!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything! I really loved Vienna and the knowledge I got and developed

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier for the paperwork I needed to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Follow the checklist that the international team at BOKU sends you before arriving, it is user friendly and very useful!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
